tour.overview:
Most visitors see the Giza pyramids in two rushed hours. This private day puts them in their story. You start at Saqqara, where around 4,700 years ago the architect Imhotep stacked six stone platforms into the Step Pyramid of King Djoser – the first large building ever made of cut stone. You go on to Memphis, the capital of the pharaohs for most of three thousand years, now a palm grove where a colossal statue of Ramesses II lies in the shade. And you finish at Giza, where the idea reached its peak in the Great Pyramid of Khufu, the only surviving wonder of the ancient world, and the Sphinx that guards it.

Your guide is a licensed Egyptologist who reads the hieroglyphs with you, explains how the pyramids were built and why the form changed, and takes you to the quieter corners: the painted tombs of Old Kingdom officials at Saqqara, the Valley Temple beside the Sphinx, and the desert viewpoint where all three Giza pyramids line up. Lunch is at a local restaurant between the sites.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and finish: your hotel in Cairo or Giza
• Type: private tour with car, driver and licensed Egyptologist guide
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; walking on sand and uneven ground

WHAT YOU SEE
• Saqqara: the Step Pyramid of Djoser and Old Kingdom tombs.
• Memphis: the open-air museum, the colossus of Ramesses II and the alabaster sphinx.
• Giza: the pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, the Great Sphinx and the Valley Temple.

WHY THIS TOUR WORKS
Seeing the sites in historical order, from the first pyramid to the greatest, makes the day make sense. Starting at Saqqara also means you reach Giza after the morning coach groups have left, in softer light.

WHO IT IS FOR
First-time visitors to Egypt, families with children who love ancient history, photographers, and anyone who wants more than a quick photo at the pyramids.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the museums, mosques and bazaars of Cairo, take our Grand Egyptian Museum and Old Cairo tour. For temples and tombs in the south, see our Luxor tours.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Wear comfortable shoes, a hat and sunglasses, and bring sunscreen and some small notes for tips and toilets. Entry inside the Great Pyramid and some special tombs needs an extra ticket; your guide will advise whether it is worth it on the day.

days.name: Saqqara, Memphis and the Giza pyramids
days.description:
What to expect: a private day following the pyramids from the first to the greatest, with an Egyptologist guide, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:00 and drive south along the Nile through farmland and villages to Saqqara, the great cemetery of ancient Memphis, about 45 minutes from central Cairo. Here, around 2670 BC, the architect Imhotep built the Step Pyramid for King Djoser: six stone platforms stacked one on another, rising about 60 metres, with a vast enclosure of courts and shrines – the first monumental building in stone in human history. Walk through the colonnaded entrance and the Heb-Sed court, then visit one or two of the decorated tombs of Old Kingdom nobles nearby, whose walls show daily life 4,500 years ago in sharp relief: fishing, farming, cattle, bakers and boat builders. Your guide reads the scenes and the hieroglyphs with you.

A short drive takes you to Memphis, the capital founded around 3100 BC by the first pharaoh to unite Upper and Lower Egypt. Little of the city survives above the palm groves, but the open-air museum holds a colossal limestone statue of Ramesses II, about 10 metres long, lying on its back under a gallery, and an alabaster sphinx. Lunch is at a local restaurant on the way back to Giza.

In the afternoon reach the Giza plateau. The Great Pyramid of Khufu, built around 2560 BC, was originally about 146 metres high and remained the tallest building on earth for nearly four thousand years. Your guide explains how it was planned and built, and you see the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure beside it. Then go down to the Great Sphinx, carved from the bedrock of the plateau, and the Valley Temple of Khafre with its massive granite pillars. Finish at the panoramic viewpoint in the desert, where all the pyramids line up for the classic photograph, before the drive back to your hotel at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate)
08:00 – Hotel pick-up.
09:00 – Saqqara: Step Pyramid of Djoser and Old Kingdom tombs (about 2 hours).
11:15 – Memphis open-air museum (about 45 minutes).
12:30 – Lunch at a local restaurant.
13:45 – Giza plateau: Great Pyramid, Khafre and Menkaure.
15:00 – The Great Sphinx and the Valley Temple.
15:45 – Panoramic viewpoint.
16:30 – Return to your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Inside the plateau, visitors move between viewpoints on official electric shuttles or on foot; we follow the current rules.
• Entry inside the Great Pyramid and special tombs costs extra and is limited; your guide advises on the day.
• Camel or horse rides at Giza can be arranged with licensed operators; agree the price before you get on.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed Egyptologist guide, entrance tickets to Saqqara, Memphis and the Giza plateau, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up.
NOT INCLUDED: entry inside the pyramids and special tombs, camel rides, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose your date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only once your tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes, the general tickets to Saqqara, Memphis and the Giza plateau. Entry inside the Great Pyramid and some special tombs needs an extra ticket.

faq.question: Is it worth going inside the Great Pyramid?
faq.answer: It is an unforgettable climb through narrow, steep, hot passages to a bare granite chamber. If you are claustrophobic or have knee problems, the tombs at Saqqara are a better choice.

faq.question: Is the guide an Egyptologist?
faq.answer: Yes. All our guides in Egypt are licensed by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities and studied Egyptology.

faq.question: Why start at Saqqara?
faq.answer: It follows history from the first pyramid to the greatest, and Giza is quieter and in better light in the afternoon.

faq.question: Can we ride a camel at Giza?
faq.answer: Yes, with licensed operators near the panoramic viewpoint. We can arrange a short ride; always agree the price before you get on.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children usually love the pyramids, the Sphinx and the camels. The guide keeps the pace easy and the stories lively.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, light clothing, a hat and sunglasses. The sites are in the open desert with little shade.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, an Egyptian lunch at a local restaurant between Memphis and Giza. Vegetarian options are always available.

faq.question: Can I do this on a layover?
faq.answer: Yes, with at least 9 hours between flights and an Egyptian visa. We pick you up and drop you at Cairo International Airport.

faq.question: Can we add the Grand Egyptian Museum?
faq.answer: Yes. The museum is next to the Giza plateau; we can swap Memphis for two hours in the museum, or make it a separate day.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: October to April. From May to September it is very hot; we start earlier and keep the afternoon at Giza short.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
